subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw provide a generic framework-authenticated provenance contract while the bundled memory plugin owns default review/influence enforcement, or should provenance and enforcement both remain extension-owned?
rationale: The repository policy requires core to remain plugin-agnostic, but the requested security property spans framework ingestion and default-memory retrieval. Choosing the durable owner boundary determines the API, migration scope, config surface, and which optional backends must participate.

options.title: Generic provenance plus memory-core policy
options.body: Add a narrow framework-assigned origin contract, then let the bundled memory plugin persist and enforce review/influence state for its own default path.

options.title: Extension-owned policy only
options.body: Expose only existing extension seams and require each memory backend or external MCP integration to implement provenance and influence controls independently.

options.title: Pause for an RFC
options.body: Defer implementation until maintainers approve a cross-backend provenance and upgrade contract covering persistence, retrieval, and plugin SDK compatibility.

recommendation.title: Generic provenance plus memory-core policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow framework-assigned origin contract, then let the bundled memory plugin persist and enforce review/influence state for its own default path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the prior source-backed review and are the strongest available routing candidate for the memory-contract product boundary.
